records.note: Alpha Centauri A reviewed physical parameters. Akeson et al. (2021) combine the revised orbital parallax with published angular diameter and bolometric flux measurements for the mass, radius, and luminosity. Kervella et al. (2017) derive the effective temperature from interferometry and bolometric flux. Morel (2018) measures [Fe/H] in a differential HARPS abundance analysis. Joyce & Chaboyer (2018) infer the shared system age from classical and asteroseismic constraints.

qualityFlags: bolometric flux plus revised orbital parallax

records.note: Luhman 16 A reviewed component parameters. Bedin et al. (2024) measure the individual dynamical mass. Lodieu et al. (2015) derive the resolved temperature and bolometric luminosity from spectroscopy and the spectral energy distribution. The displayed age is the Oceanus moving-group age supported, but not established, by Bedin et al.; their evolutionary-model comparison still shows component-age tension. Resolved V photometry is from Boffin et al. (2014), Table 2, observed 2013-06-16 (uncertainty 0.10 mag). Ishikawa et al. (2025), Table 2, provide a separate component radial-velocity observation from 2018-04-21 to 2018-06-29; it includes orbital motion and is not adopted for the long-horizon space-motion vector.

qualityFlags: asymmetric uncertainty represented by its larger side
35.4 +/- 0.2 Jupiter masses converted to solar masses

photometry.scope: Resolved Johnson V photometry of Luhman 16 A; FORS2 v_HIGH, calibrated with standards E5 and LTT4816. Snapshot photometry; not the unresolved pair.

radialVelocityObservation.uncertainty_kind: Unbiased weighted standard deviation across 46 spectral orders; not a formal standard error.
radialVelocityObservation.scope: Resolved Luhman 16 A spectroscopic radial velocity from barycentric-corrected IGRINS spectra. Includes component orbital motion; not the binary systemic velocity. Display-only observation; not combined with the different-epoch catalog proper motion to infer bulk space motion.

records.note: WISE 0855-0714 reviewed bolometric luminosity. Zapatero Osorio et al. (2016) fit the 0.89-22.09 micron spectral energy distribution with solar-metallicity atmosphere models. Their broad 2-10 Jupiter-mass and 1-12 Gyr ranges are retained in provenance rather than collapsed into misleading scalar mass or age values.

records.note: Sirius A reviewed physical parameters from Bond et al. (2017). The radius is interferometric, the mass dynamical, and the luminosity and temperature use the adopted parallax. The age and bulk [Fe/H] are stellar-evolution model results; the bulk metallicity is used instead of Sirius A's diffusion-altered Am photospheric abundance.

qualityFlags: bulk [Fe/H] midpoint of -0.13 to -0.07 model range
midpoint of independent 237-247 Myr model results

records.note: Sirius B reviewed physical parameters from Bond et al. (2017). The mass is dynamical; temperature, radius, and luminosity come from HST/STIS atmosphere and absolute-flux fitting. The displayed age is the total evolutionary age, not merely the 126 Myr white-dwarf cooling time. Photospheric metallicity remains intentionally blank for this pure-hydrogen white dwarf.

Tau Ceti reviewed physical parameters. Korolik et al. (2023) combine CHARA interferometry and EXPRES spectroscopy; their measured temperature supersedes the earlier spectral-class estimate, and their luminosity is reported in the paper's literature-comparison table. Di Folco et al. (2004) infer the adopted age from stellar-evolution modelling. Pagano et al. (2015) measure [Fe/H] from high-resolution MIKE spectra.

qualityFlags: spectroscopic surface gravity plus interferometric radius
CHARA limb-darkened diameter plus Gaia parallax

records.note: Procyon A component parameters: dynamical mass and preferred 2.70 Gyr high-core-overshoot age from Bond et al. (2015); age is model-dependent (alternative tracks 1.673 and 1.817 Gyr). Chiavassa et al. (2012) provide 6591 +/- 43 K and the 2.019 solar interferometric radius; the alternative bolometric flux gives 6556 +/- 84 K. Photospheric [Fe/H] is the differential 3D LTE result of Allende Prieto et al. (2002).

records.note: LAWD 37: McGill et al. (2023) gravitational microlensing mass and DQ atmospheric-fit temperature/radius. Carbon abundance is not ordinary stellar [Fe/H]. The reported 1.15 Gyr age is a cooling age; no total stellar age is inferred.

Stein 2051 B: Sahu et al. (2017) gravitational microlensing mass and model-atmosphere photometric temperature/radius from the supplementary material. The total age is reported as a 1.9-3.6 Gyr range and remains in this note; no scalar midpoint or ordinary stellar [Fe/H] is invented.
